newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA HAS NEW PUBLIC TRANSPORT PLAN -MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA HAS NEW PUBLIC TRANSPORT PLAN -MINISTER.

text.p: Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said on Wednesday South Africa should have a public transport system in place in three to four years that would allow decreased dependence on the private car.

He told a news conference that regulatory changes in the bus, rail and mini-bus taxi sectors "should take us to the point where in three to four years we've got a playing field where we can look at public transport coming together as an intermodal facility".
"(Then) we can address the larger problems where the system has favoured the private car user."
He said a team probing the mini-bus taxi industry, chaired by Dipak Patel, was trying to encourage the industry to switch to diesel and to use larger 20- to 25-seater midi-buses.
Patel said many of the midi-buses were already being imported but local assemblers Mercedes-Benz and Toyota were considering getting into the market for these vehicles.
"Two objectives are being achieved: for the industry itself in terms of viability and economic sustainability, we're going to start seeing an increasing economy of scale," Patel said.
"From a traffic congestion point of view, we're going to see a larger variety of vehicle sizes and types coming onto the market which can help the transport industry to better plan."
Maharaj said his department was negotiating with unions on the possibility of starting a demonstration concession project on passenger trains.

"Our target is to reach agreement by mid-1998," he said. "Our hope is that at the end of this road, passenger services provided by rail will be done on full concessioning over the entire network," he said.
